title: Check yourself: static initialisation and hiding

questions.stem: In the page's `StaticTest`, `x` is declared as `10`, a static block above `main` adds 5 to it, and a static block below `main` divides it by 3. What does `main` print?

options.says: That would need the lower block to run first (10 / 3 = 3, then + 5); the page says blocks run in textual order.
Static blocks run in the order they appear, all before main: 10 + 5 = 15, then 15 / 3 = 5.
That would need the block below main to run after main; the page says every static block runs before main.

questions.stem: A subclass declares a static method with exactly the signature of a static method of its superclass. What does the page say this does?

options.text: It hides the inherited one instead of overriding it
options.says: The page says a static method with the same signature in a subclass hides the parent's method rather than overriding it.

options.text: It overrides the inherited one, as instance methods do
options.says: The page says static methods cannot be overridden; they are hidden.

options.text: It is refused by the compiler as a duplicate one
options.says: The page describes the result as hiding, which compiles; it is not a duplicate declaration.
